processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloys were made of high-purity elements Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%), C (99.99%) and Be (99.99%) and melted into alloy ingots in a vacuum induction melting furnace under a high-purity argon atmosphere; the obtained ingot has a diameter of 60 mm and a thickness of 30 mm. The as-cast state is the terminal state with no heat treatment and no thermal deformation applied (the 1050 °C hot rolling described in the paper belongs to the separate rolled state, not this sample).

structures.overall_structure: As-cast 1.5Be steel is a dual-phase austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) structure with randomly distributed Be–Fe compound (beryllium compound) precipitates; ferrite is evenly distributed in the austenite matrix. In the OM the bright blocky/vermiform δ islands are finer and more fragmented than in 1.0Be and are separated by a more continuous dark Be–Fe compound network.

phases_present.morphology: darker matrix in OM; γ(111)(200)(220)(311)(222) reflections in XRD
bright blocky/vermiform islands embedded in the darker γ matrix; in 1.5Be the islands are finer and more fragmented than in 1.0Be; δ(200) reflection at ~2θ 44.5°
needle-like, rod-like, plate-shaped and 'ancient Chinese character'-shaped compounds; forms a continuous dark network between the δ islands in as-cast 1.5Be; randomly distributed

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: The ferrite grain size of the 1.5Be as-cast steel is evidently smaller than that of the 1.0Be content (no numeric value reported for the as-cast state).

precipitates.distribution: Most of them are polymerised to form a large needle-peak structure; large Be–Fe precipitates intersect horizontally and vertically; coarse needle-/plate-shaped and blocky lath-like morphologies in BF-TEM
Be2Fe peaks appear in the XRD pattern of 1.5Be as-cast steel
Be11Fe lines present in the 1.5Be as-cast XRD trace (around which the Be2Fe and Be12Fe peaks appear)
BeC markers appear on the 1.5Be as-cast XRD trace
Selective-area diffraction of the 1.5Be as-cast matrix revealed the AlFe3 diffraction spot; blocky lath-like morphology

interfaces.phase_evolution: With increasing Be content the austenite region shrinks (Al and Be are ferrite-stabilising); Be–Fe phase compounds and ferrite form. In the as-cast 1.0Be and 1.5Be steels the ferrite content decreases relative to lower Be because the increasing Be–Fe phase encroaches on the austenite matrix and reduces austenite content. Be initially forms compounds rather than ferrite; above the austenite solubility (<1% Be) excess Be precipitates as compounds and stabilises ferrite.
interfaces.interface_notes: Beryllium precipitates in the shape of ancient Chinese characters appear at the boundary between austenite and ferrite in the as-cast microstructure; these precipitates are widely distributed and cross vertically and horizontally. When remaining Be cannot dissolve in austenite it precipitates on ferrite in the form of spot-like compounds.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured with FM-ARS9000 Vickers hardness tester; matrix hardness measured with a 500 gf force tap; each sample tested using a 15×5 matrix and the average of 25 points taken as the microhardness value.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα X-ray tube (D/MAX-2500/PC; ASTM D5380-93[2014])
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 2θ range 20°–100°, scanning speed 2° per minute, continuous scanning; specimen polished with #150–#800 sandpaper and ultrasonically cleaned in alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase composition of the as-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–1.5Be steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 1.5Be consists of austenite (γ) + ferrite (δ) + partial precipitates; the δ(110)/(200) reflection at ~2θ 44.67° grows with Be; Be2Fe, Be12Fe, Be11Fe and BeC peaks appear on the 1.5Be trace

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Axiovert 200 MAT optical microscope; specimens cut by electric spark, prepared per standard metallographic methods with #400–#5000 waterproof sandpapers, 0.5 μm diamond suspension polish, etched with 8% nitrate alcohol solution
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dual-phase structure with bright blocky/vermiform δ islands in a darker γ matrix and dark inter-island 'Beryllium compound'; in 1.5Be the δ islands appear finer and more fragmented than in 1.0Be

characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JE-2100F TEM, operating voltage 200 kV; TEM sample thinned to 40 μm with waterproof sandpaper then twin-jet electropolished in 10% perchloric acid + 90% ethanol at 26.5 V and −20 °C
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: As-cast 1.5Be steel; 1 µm scale bars; SAED [011] zone axis for AlFe3
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe precipitates and diffraction spots in the as-cast 1.5Be steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Coarse needle-/plate-shaped and blocky lath-like precipitates attributed to Be12Fe; the 1.5Be matrix selected-area diffraction revealed an AlFe3 [011] pattern (reflections 111, 1̄11, 200)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; 500 gf force tap for matrix; 15×5 matrix with average of 25 points
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure microhardness of the as-cast matrix (austenite), ferrite and Be-Fe phase
characterization_methods.key_findings: 1.5Be as-cast: austenite 479.74 ±11.99 HV, ferrite 452.54 ±12.33 HV, Be-Fe phase 477.16 ±14.14 HV

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–Be binary system; temperature T = 0–1800 °C; composition axis Fe/(Be+Fe) = 0–1 (mol/mol)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used to rationalise that almost no Be is soluble in austenite at room temperature and that Be–Fe compounds (FeBe12 ≈ 0.13, FeBe5 ≈ 0.17, FeBe2 ≈ 0.33) form, consistent with the observed compound precipitation

analytical_models.model_name: Relative atomic size factor / solid-solution type criterion
analytical_models.equation_role: Determines the solid-solution type of solute atoms in the Fe matrix (infinite solid solution requires <8% atomic radius difference and identical crystal structure)
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. 3: Δr = |(r_A − r_B)/r_A|. Mn, Al and Be form substitutional solid solutions; C forms an interstitial solid solution. Be (111 pm) is smaller than Fe so causes inward lattice shrinkage; Al (143 pm) is larger and causes outward lattice expansion.

unmapped_findings: Density of the 1.5Be alloy: Table 3 lists ρ = 6.29 ±0.05 g/cm³ for 1.5Be under the column group 'Rolling states', and the conclusion (b0099) and Fig. 20 quote 6.29 g/cm³; the abstract (b0009) separately quotes 'about approximately 6.25 g/cm³' for the 1.5Be steel. The only tabulated density is explicitly attributed to the rolled state (Table 3), so it cannot be unambiguously assigned to the as-cast 1.5Be sample.
As-cast 1.5Be density was not separately reported; density measured by Archimedes drainage (Eqs. 1–2) with a high-precision balance (0.01 g) and averaged over three independent measurements.

DSC phase-transformation peak for 1.5Be = 1154.8 °C, taken from heating curves 'after homogenisation' (Fig. 6); this measurement state (homogenised) is not the as-cast state, so it is recorded here rather than in the as-cast properties.

Lattice-distortion fact (general to the alloy): substitutional Be (smaller than Fe) causes inward lattice shrinkage (lattice distortion), whereas Al (larger than Fe) causes outward lattice expansion; the resulting lattice distortion of Be does not effectively reduce density even though Be itself has a low density of ~1.87 g/cm³.
The 5–10 μm precipitate size quoted in the paper refers to the as-cast 0.5Be steel (Be-Fe/Be12Fe), not the 1.5Be sample.
